# **1\. Introduction** 

The rapid growth of digital streaming platforms has fundamentally changed the way people are interacting and using television content. With thousands of titles available across dozens of services such as Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic and etc.) users increasingly rely on centralized databases, community ratings and recommendations that navigate the way they interact with each movie or TV show. Building a system that addresses this need presents a rich and realistic engineering challenge, one that goes from database design, backend API development, user credentials, and responsive frontend implementation.

The goal of this project is to apply theoretical knowledge to a practical. This entire software development lifecycle covered everything from requirements and system planning through iterative development and testing.

Development follows Agile methodology. Allowing the team to deliver working functionality at each stage rather than treating final submission as the sole point of completion, this approach reflects industry practices and ensures planning, implementation and quality assurance remain continuous activities throughout the project.

In this document we will explain what is being built, why it is being built, and how the team plans to build it. The sections that follow present the project description, high-level plan, functional and non-functional requirements, and a risk analysis.

1. ## **About the Project** {#about-the-project}

Purpose  
IMDB or Internet Movie Database is a web-based application designed to give users a single, convenient destination for discovering movies and TV shows. Where they can read and write reviews, managing personal watchlists, and receive tailored content recommendations. It combines content discovery with social interaction, allowing every registered user to contribute ratings and opinions visible to the wider community.

### **1.1.2	Main Features** {#1.1.2-main-features}

\- Content Library searchable database of movies and TV shows with synopsis, cast, genre, release year, and content ratings  
\- User Authentication secure registration and login system with session management  
\- Ratings System users rate titles on a 1–10 scale and scores are calculated into a average ratings per movie  
\- Reviews system authenticated users write, edit, and delete text reviews visible to all visitors  
\- Watchlist: Each user maintains a private list of titles they plan to watch  
\- Search, filter, and Sort real-time search by title, filtering by type/genre, sorting by rating or year  
\- Admin Panel administrators add, edit, and delete content entries

### **1.1.3 Benefits**  {#1.1.3-benefits}

Users can browse, rate, and review content all within a single platform, eliminating the need to consult multiple separate services. Community-driven ratings and reviews provide a crowdsourced quality signal. A fully responsive design ensures the application works across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

### **1.1.4 Downsides** {#1.1.4-downsides}

The content library is dependent on an external API, meaning that if the API is unavailable or limited, the data shown to users may be incomplete or outdated. On top of that, allowing users to freely write reviews introduces the risk of spam or offensive content, which ideally would require a moderation system that was beyond the scope of what the team could realistically implement.

### **1.1.5 Methodology** {#1.1.5-methodology}

The project follows an Agile development approach, meaning the work is divided into three milestone-based releases rather than being delivered all at once. Each release builds on the previous one, ensuring there is always a defined deliverable at every stage and allowing the team to adjust priorities if something takes longer than expected.  
The first release focuses on planning and laying the foundation and defining requirements, writing user stories, creating UML diagrams, and establishing a high-level roadmap for the entire project. The second release moves into implementation, delivering a working initial version of the application with basic CRUD operations, a database ER diagram, and the core features that make the application usable, user registration and login, browsing movies, searching, and basic ratings. The third and final release completes the application by adding the remaining interactive features such as reviews, watchlists, user profiles, and recommendations, while also ensuring that tests are written, architectural and design patterns are properly applied, and the application is deployed and publicly accessible.  
This approach was chosen because it keeps the project manageable and each milestone has a clear scope and deadline, which reduces the risk of leaving everything to the last moment and ensures the application is always in a functional state.

## **1.3. Project Requirements** {#1.3.-project-requirements}

1. User registration 

Statement: As a new user, I want to register using my email and password so that I can use personalized features.  
Acceptance criteria: 

- The form validates that the email matches the required format.   
- Passwords should comply with certain security criteria (e.g., at least 6 symbols).  
- After successful registration, the user gets redirected to the home page.  
2. User login 

Statement: As a registered user, I want to log in to my account so that I can use my saved data.  
Acceptance criteria:

- If credentials are correct, the user logs into the system and gains access to his account.  
- If either username or password is incorrect, the system displays a proper "invalid" error message.  
3. User logout 

Statement: As a logged-in user, I want to be able to log out of my session so that my account is protected from being used by anyone else.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a separate "logout" button located in the menu.  
- After clicking it, the user session gets cleared, and he is redirected to the home page.  
4. Access user profile 

Statement: As a user, I want to view my user profile page so that I can see statistics about my interactions with the website.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The user's profile page contains a list of his movie ratings/reviews and the current "Watchlist".  
5. Edit profile 

Statement: As a user, I want to be able to edit my user data so that it will always be up-to-date.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Editable user data is accessible.  
- Changes are saved in the database upon clicking the "Save" button.

   
6\. Movies listing  
Statement: As a user, I want to view a list of movies so that I could choose something interesting to watch.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The list shows movie name, image, and rating.  
- The list loads successfully and has no broken images.  
7. Search functionality 

Statement: As a user, I want to be able to search for specific movies so that I won't have to scroll through the whole list.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The results get filtered according to text input.  
- If there are no results found, a "Not found" message should appear.  
8. Filters 

Statement: As a user, I want to filter movies according to the specified genres or their type (TV/Movie) so that I could find something to watch right now.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Users should be allowed to use multiple filters at once (e.g., "Horror" AND "Movie").  
- The list updates automatically if a filter is applied.  
9. Sorting 

Statement: As a user, I want to sort the list according to rating or the year of publication so that I can see the best or most recent movie on top of the list.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a dropdown/toggle to sort movies.  
- Sorting works both ways: from bottom to top, and vice versa.  
10. Movie description 

Statement: As a user, I want to read additional information about a certain movie so that I could decide whether or not to watch it.  
Acceptance criteria:

- When clicked, the movie shows a full description, rating, and actors' names.  
11. Paginating 

Statement: As a user, I want the movies' list to be paginated to avoid loading a long list.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There are Next/Previous buttons for page navigation.  
- Each page displays a predefined number of entries.

12\. Rate a movie  
Statement: As a user, I want to rate a certain movie using a scale from 1 to 10 so that I could keep track of my favorite ones.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a scale or a star-based input (1-10)  
- The rating is saved in the database and bound to the user's ID.  
13. Editing rating 

Statement: As a user, I want to be able to change my rating of a certain movie if needed.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The user should be allowed to modify the rating.  
- The new rating replaces the previous one in the database.  
14. Deleting rating 

Statement: As a user, I want to delete the rating I've assigned to a particular movie if needed.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a "Delete" or "Remove rating" option on each card.  
- The rating is removed from the database.  
15. Writing a review 

Statement: As a user, I want to leave a comment on a certain movie to express my opinion about it.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a text input field for writing reviews.  
- Reviews are saved in the database and shown publicly on a movie card.  
16. Editing review 

Statement: As a user, I want to edit the text of my review after posting it if there are typos or other issues.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The user sees an "Edit" button next to his post.  
- Edited text is displayed correctly on the card.  
17. Deleting review 

Statement: As a user, I want to delete my review if needed.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Clicking the delete button deletes the review from the card/database.  
18. Community reviews 

Statement: As a user, I want to see comments left by other users about a movie so that I could see different opinions.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The reviews list contains the creator's username and post time.

19\. Add to watchlist  
Statement: As a user, I want to save movies to my "watchlist" so that I can find them later.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is an "Add to Watchlist" button on the movie card or page.  
- The movie is saved to the user's private watchlist.  
20. Removing from watchlist 

Statement: As a user, I want to be able to remove movies from my watchlist if I've already watched them or don't need it anymore.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The user sees a "remove" option.  
- Removing a movie deletes it from the watchlist instantly.  
21. Viewing watchlist 

Statement: As a user, I want to have my own watchlist page where I can see all saved movies.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There is a separate page for watching the watchlist.  
22. Recommendations 

Statement: As a user, I want to see recommendations for movies based on my previous ratings so that I could easily discover new ones.  
Acceptance criteria:

- System recommendations are made according to user's movie genre preferences or rating history matching the user's highest-rated movie genre.

23\. Admin: Adding content  
Statement: As an admin, I want to be able to add new movies so that the database would stay up to date.  
Acceptance criteria:

- The admin panel has a form to insert movie data.  
- A new entry gets saved into the database and is visible to all users.  
24. Admin: Editing content 

Statement: As an admin, I want to edit the movie data in case of mistakes in its previous description or casting.  
Acceptance criteria:

- An admin has permissions to edit the movie data freely.  
- Changes are immediately applied on all pages.  
25. Admin: Deleting content 

Statement: As an admin, I want to be able to delete some movies if they are no longer relevant or got mistakenly inserted.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Deleting a movie removes it from the database together with all related data.

Non-functional

26\. Speed performance  
Statement: As a user, I want the site pages to be loaded fast so that my experience is not disturbed by any problems.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Main pages (home, search) load in less than 2 sec.  
- APIs are optimized to increase speed.  
27. Security of the data 

Statement: As a user, I want my data to be secured and safe from theft.  
Acceptance criteria:

- Access to data is secured by authentication (tokens/sessions).  
28. System reliability 

Statement: As a user, I want the site to be reliable and error-prone.  
Acceptance criteria:

- There are minimal failures, the system works almost at all times.

\- If any problem occurs, the user sees a friendly "something went wrong" message.

# **2\. Project Structure** 

## **2.1. Technologies** {#2.1.-technologies}

Backend Node.js was used as the runtime environment and Express.js as the web framework for building the REST API. The backend handles all routing, authentication middleware, input validation, and business logic. The following additional libraries were used:

- bcrypt.js  for hashing user passwords before storing them in the database  
- jsonwebtoken (JWT) for generating and verifying authentication tokens  
- express-validator for validating and sanitizing incoming request data  
- dotenv for managing environment variables such as the database URI and JWT secret  
- Nodemon is used during development to automatically restart the server on file changes  
- cors to allow cross-origin requests between the frontend and backend

Two frontend implementations were built for this project:

- React 18 with React Router was used as the primary frontend, organized into reusable components (Navbar, MovieCard, StarRating, and ReviewForm) and page components (Home, Login, Register, MovieDetail, Profile, WatchlistPage, and AdminPanel). Axios was used as the HTTP client for all API calls, wrapped in a centralized services/api.js file. A custom useAuth hook manages global authentication state.  
- Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were built as a secondary frontend, served directly by Express. This version includes all the same pages and is fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile screens.

The MongoDB database was used as the database, with Mongoose as the ODM (Object Document Mapper) for defining schemas, enforcing data types, and handling relationships between collections.

External API Integration The TMDb (The Movie Database) API was integrated optionally for seeding the database with real movie data, including titles, overviews, poster images, genres, and release dates. The integration is handled through an Adapter pattern in backend/services/tmdbAdapter.js, which transforms the external API response into the internal Movie schema format.

Testing, Jest, and Supertest were used to write unit and integration tests for the backend. Tests run against a separate test database (imdb\_test) and cover authentication, movie CRUD operations, ratings, reviews, and watchlist functionality.

Coding Standard: The team followed the Airbnb JavaScript Style Guide across both the backend and frontend. The key conventions applied were:

- camelCase for all variable and function names  
- PascalCase for React components and Mongoose model names  
- Single quotes for all strings  
- Two-space indentation throughout all files  
- async/await used consistently instead of raw Promise chains or callbacks  
- One component or module per file, with clear and descriptive naming

  ## **2.2. Database Entities**

The application uses MongoDB with Mongoose. The database contains the following five collections:

- Users store registered user accounts, including username, email, hashed password, role (user or admin), avatar URL, and timestamps for account creation  
- movies: the main content entity of the application, storing the title, overview, poster image URL, release date, content type (movie or TV show), and computed fields for average rating and total rating count  
- reviews stores text-based reviews written by users about specific movies. Each review is linked to a user and a movie via reference IDs, and includes the review text and timestamps for creation and last edit  
- Ratings store the numeric score (between 1 and 10\) that a user assigns to a specific movie. The system enforces one rating per user per movie, and automatically updates the movie's average rating when a rating is added, changed, or removed  
- watchlist: a junction collection that tracks which movies each user has saved to their personal watchlist, storing references to both the user and the movie along with the date the item was added  
- genres stores genre categories (e.g. Horror, Drama, Comedy) that are associated with movies through the movie\_genre join collection  
- Actors store information about cast members, including name, biography, and birth year, linked to movies through the movie\_actor join collection  
- movie\_genre: a join collection that maps the many-to-many relationship between movies and genres, storing a movieId and genreId reference pair for each association  
- movie\_actor: a join collection that maps the many-to-many relationship between movies and actors, storing a movieId and actorId reference pair for each association
